cards.explanation: The kingdom goes to Jehoram because he was the firstborn. Friends, verse 3 says their father gave the kingdom to Jehoram for that reason. The other brothers got many gifts of silver, gold and precious things, plus fortified cities in Judah. But the kingdom itself went to Jehoram.

The answer is False. Verse 6 says Jehoram "…did evil in the sight of the LORD." He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, and he married a daughter of Ahab. So the text says he did evil, not right, friends.

The other reason is His covenant with David. Verse 7 says the LORD was unwilling to destroy the house of David "…because of the covenant He had made with David…" The verse also gives His promise to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever. So the reason is what God had promised, not how Jehoram was acting.

The word is king. Verse 8 says Edom rebelled against the hand of Judah and "…appointed their own king." Friends, they didn't just rebel, they put someone in charge of their own. This happened in the days of Jehoram.
The answer is True. Verse 9 says Jehoram crossed into Edom with his officers and all his chariots. Not just some of the chariots, bakers, all of them.

Jehoram rises up and attacks by night. Verse 9 says that when the Edomites surrounded him and his chariot commanders, he rose up and attacked by night. Surrounded, and he got up and went at them in the dark. I would've stayed seated and asked everybody to be reasonable.

Libnah rebelled because Jehoram had forsaken the LORD. Verse 10 says Libnah rebelled against his hand at the same time "…because Jehoram had forsaken the LORD, the God of his fathers." Friends, the text puts the reason right there in the same verse.

The message reaches Jehoram in a letter. Verse 12 says a letter came to Jehoram from Elijah the prophet. It opens with "This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says…" So the message came as a letter, bakers, and it speaks for the LORD.

The kings are Jehoshaphat and Asa king of Judah. The letter says, "You have not walked in the ways of your father Jehoshaphat or of Asa king of Judah…" Jehoshaphat was Jehoram's own father. So the letter points him back to the kings of Judah he didn't follow.

The answer is True. The letter says Jehoram killed his brothers, "…your father’s family, who were better than you." Friends, those are the same brothers from the start of the chapter. This is a heavy line, and the letter doesn't dress it up.
The answer is False. Verse 15 says Jehoram "…yourself will suffer from a severe illness…" It's a disease of his bowels, day after day. The letter says he won't come through it unharmed, friends.

The LORD stirs up the Philistines and Arabs. Verse 16 says the LORD stirred against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and Arabs who lived near the Cushites. Those are the two peoples the text names, bakers. They went to war against Judah after that.

The only son left is Jehoahaz, his youngest. Verse 17 says "not a son was left to him except Jehoahaz, his youngest." The invaders carried off the king's other sons along with his wives. Only Jehoahaz stayed. It's a sad verse, friends.

The LORD is the one who afflicts him. Verse 18 says, "After all this, the LORD afflicted Jehoram with an incurable disease of the bowels." Elijah's letter had named this very disease. The text tells us plainly who did it, friends.
The answer is False. Verse 19 says his people did not make a fire in his honor, as they had done for his fathers. His fathers were honored that way, but he wasn't. It's a quiet, heavy line, friends.

The word is kings. Verse 20 says Jehoram "…was buried in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings." He was buried in the right city but not in the royal tombs. The text says he died to no one's regret, friends.
